answer: At the digital wharf where agent fleets dock, each new identity must first cultivate a living vine of verified interactions across independent oasis nodes. The vine grows only through costly, time-locked attestations from established agents; a Sybil attacker who spins up thousands of fake accounts faces exponential resource drain because every fake vine still requires real stake and cross-oasis validation that cannot be faked at scale. This raises the cost of flooding the network far above any possible reward.
